title: add-vpc-control-plane-terraform-multi-az-interface-endpoints-peering-route53
author: Leah Martinez
body:
Summary: Add Terraform support and installer hooks to provision a multi-AZ VPC control plane environment. This PR introduces a reusable terraform module for interface endpoints, security groups, subnet automation, cross-account VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zone peering. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private have requested out-of-the-box multi-AZ networking that follows our security posture (least-privilege SGs, interface endpoints for control plane services) and simplifies on-prem/aws hybrid setups with Route53 peering. This enables a single Terraform path for private control plane provisioning and reduces manual steps in the private-installer. Changes included: 1) Terraform module: modules/vpc-control-plane - new module that provisions: - multi-AZ private subnets with configurable CIDR allocation - interface endpoints for S3, STS, EC2 (for ECR pulls), and common AWS services used by the control plane - interface and gateway endpoints where appropriate - security groups with explicit ingress/egress allowing only control-plane CIDR and management CIDR - VPC peering resources and acceptance (cross-account optional via flags) - Route53 private hosted zone association and zone peering resources 2) Private installer integration: private-installer/terraform/ - added example usage and outputs expected by the installer (control_plane_endpoint_dns, management_subnets, endpoint_ids) 3) Helm chart and upgrade hooks: redwood-helm-charts/control-plane - added values schema to accept pre-provisioned endpoint IDs and security group IDs; added post-upgrade hook to reconcile DNS records in AWS Route53 to avoid drift during upgrades 4) Documentation and quickstart: redwood-docs/private/vpc-setup.md - step-by-step using the new module, migration notes for existing users 5) Tests and validation: perf-canary/terraform-smoke - simple plan/apply/verify pipeline used in CI to validate module idempotency and Route53 association. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented with variables + outputs - [x] Installer consumes module outputs - [x] Helm values and hooks updated to accept pre-provisioned resources - [x] Integration tests added to CI smoke job - [x] Docs updated and sample usage added Backwards compatibility: This is opt-in. Existing private deployments continue to use the current installer behavior. New boolean var 'use_preprovisioned_networking' toggles the installer path. Migration notes: For existing customers who want to adopt the module we provide a migration script (scripts/migrate-to-module.sh) which exports existing subnet/sg/zone IDs and can be used to populate TF state. Testing: Ran full plan/apply in sandbox (account: redwood-sandbox-priv), exercised cross-account peering acceptance flow using temporary IAM role. CI initially had one flaky test (route53-association) which was mitigated by adding a retry loop in the smoke test. Rollout plan: 1) Merge module to main behind feature flag 2) Run migration script for internal QA clusters 3) Offer as opt-in in release notes and docs 4) After stabilization enable as promoted example in private-installer quickstart Security review: SG rules are minimal and logged; IAM role required to accept peering connections is documented. Related: ENG-1874 (multi-az networking), OPS-402 (installer automation). Notes for reviewers: Focus on the terraform module variable validation, the helm values compatibility, and the upgrade hook idempotency. Small illustrative terraform snippet (example usage): module "control_plane_vpc" { source = "../../modules/vpc-control-plane" vpc_id = var.vpc_id azs = var.azs management_cidr = var.management_cidr enable_cross_account_peering = true peer_account_id = var.peer_account_id }

This PR intentionally keeps defaults conservative (no automatic peering acceptance unless explicitly enabled). Known limitations: - Cross-region Route53 peering is out of scope for this change - On-prem DNS integration beyond Route53 (e.g. bind, AD-integrated DNS) is a follow-up.
commits: terraform(modules): add vpc-control-plane module with interface endpoint support and outputs
installer: wire module outputs into private-installer example and add migration script
helm(control-plane): add values for preprovisioned endpoints and post-upgrade dns reconciliation hook
docs: add vpc-setup quickstart and migration notes
ci: add smoke test for terraform plan/apply/verify route53 association
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Please add validation to ensure at least 2 AZs are provided when enable_cross_account_peering = true. Also can we tighten egress rules for the control plane SG?
Leah Martinez: Added validation in variables.tf (min_items = 2) and tightened egress to only necessary AWS endpoints; pushed new commit 3/5
Monica Ruiz: Verified Terraform plan output looks clean for both fresh and existing state; left a nit on output naming (control_plane_endpoint_dns -> control_plane_dns_name)
Leah Martinez: Renamed output to control_plane_dns_name and updated installer consumption; thanks!
Ethan Kim: CI smoke test failed once due to eventual consistency on route53 association. Recommend a retry/backoff — added in a follow-up commit.
Leah Martinez: Added retry loop in perf-canary test and re-ran CI; all checks passed.
OPS team (comment): Documented IAM requirement for cross-account peering acceptance; flagged for security review.
release_notes:
- Add terraform module 'vpc-control-plane' to provision multi-AZ control plane networking with interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, and Route53 private hosted zone association.
- Private installer: opt-in support for pre-provisioned networking via 'use_preprovisioned_networking'.
- Helm: control-plane chart accepts pre-provisioned endpoint IDs and includes a post-upgrade hook to reconcile Route53 records.
- Migration script provided for existing deployments.
notes: This is an infrastructure-only change; no model/service API changes. Module is intended to be reusable by partners and internal deployments.
